questions.scenario: It's winter in Delhi/North India and the AQI (smog) is terrible. What is your first reaction?

options.text: Wetting thick towels to seal the door gaps and physically placing air-purifying plants (like Snake plants) all over the balcony.
Opening the AQI app constantly to track the PM2.5 levels and analyzing the graph of when the pollution spikes the most.
Taking dramatic, moody photos of the smog-covered city streets to post an aesthetic awareness story on Instagram.
Starting a campaign in your society WhatsApp group to pool cars for school drops and ban the burning of dry leaves.

questions.scenario: Your school is organizing a massive Tree Plantation Drive before the monsoon. What's your role?

options.text: Getting your hands dirty digging the soil, adding the khaad (manure), and making sure the sapling's roots are planted perfectly.
Measuring the exact distance between the pits so the growing trees don't compete for underground water and nutrients.
Painting the clay pots with beautiful traditional Warli art and making the new garden look incredibly stunning.
Collecting Rs. 50 from every student to buy the saplings in bulk from the local nursery and assigning watering duties.

questions.scenario: You are on a family safari trip to Jim Corbett or Ranthambore National Park. What are you doing in the gypsy?

options.text: Standing up, scanning the dirt for fresh tiger pugmarks (footprints), and trying to identify the warning calls of monkeys.
Noting down the exact timings, temperatures, and zones where animal sightings are statistically the highest for the day.
Hanging onto your DSLR camera, waiting for the perfect lighting to get a National Geographic-style shot of a deer.
Observing how the safari resort operates and asking if they share their eco-tourism profits with the local tribal guides.

questions.scenario: Your city's municipality enforces strict sorting of 'Dry' and 'Wet' waste at home. How do you handle it?

options.text: Physically separating the dirty plastic wrappers from the vegetable peels into the green and blue dustbins yourself.
Tracking how many kilograms of plastic your family actually generates per month to see if it's increasing or decreasing.
Designing cool, color-coded, handmade labels for the dustbins with little drawings so the house-help easily understands them.
Explaining the municipal corporation's fine system to your parents to ensure strict compliance and zero penalties for the house.

questions.scenario: A pigeon or sparrow makes a nest on your AC compressor or balcony ledge. What do you do?

options.text: Carefully placing a bowl of bajra and water near the nest every morning without scaring the bird away.
Trying to identify the exact species by looking up its feather colors, beak shape, and egg incubation period online.
Setting up your phone on a tripod to record a beautiful time-lapse video of the eggs eventually hatching.
Laying down strict rules for your younger sibling and parents not to open that balcony door to ensure the bird's safety.

questions.scenario: There is a severe water shortage in your locality during the peak Indian summer. How do you react?

options.text: Grabbing a wrench or M-Seal to physically fix that one leaking bathroom tap that no one else is bothering to repair.
Calculating exactly how many liters of water the family wastes if a tap drips all night, to prove a point.
Coming up with a catchy slogan and drawing a poster to stick next to the society pump to remind people to save water.
Imposing a strict 'half-bucket bath only' rule in the house and taking charge of monitoring the overhead tank's water limit.

questions.scenario: It's Diwali time! Your friends are debating whether to buy firecrackers. What is your input?

options.text: Volunteering to go out the next morning with a broom to physically clean up the toxic burnt cracker waste from the street.
Explaining the exact difference in decibel limits and sulfur dioxide emissions between 'Green Crackers' and normal ones.
Arranging a gorgeous, aesthetic display of hundreds of clay diyas to prove that light looks way better than loud explosions.
Managing the group's budget to buy only eco-friendly items and organizing a 'No-Cracker Oath' for the entire society.

questions.scenario: You are accompanying your mother to the crowded local Sabzi Mandi (vegetable market). What do you focus on?

options.text: Carrying your heavy cloth jhola around the muddy market to physically avoid taking even a single plastic polythene.
Comparing the prices of organic versus chemically farmed tomatoes to figure out the exact percentage price difference.
Admiring the beautiful, vibrant colors of the fresh purple brinjals and red carrots stacked perfectly on the wooden carts.
Telling the sabzi-wala how much money he could save if he stopped buying plastic bags and switched to cheap newspaper ones.

questions.scenario: Heavy monsoon rains have caused serious flooding in parts of Mumbai or Assam. How do you follow the news?

options.text: Wishing you could wade through the water to rescue stranded street dogs and move them to higher ground.
Checking the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) radar maps online to predict when the red alert will finally end.
Documenting the rain hitting your windowpanes with a lo-fi Indian indie song playing in the background.
Organizing a relief fund in your school to send packets of Parle-G, blankets, and safe drinking water to the affected areas.

questions.scenario: You have to build a Working Science Model on 'Solar Energy'. What part do you naturally take over?

options.text: Wiring the tiny solar panels to a small DC motor yourself to ensure the mini fan actually spins when placed in the sun.
Calculating exactly how many kilowatts of energy a real-sized panel would generate during peak afternoon heat.
Making the cardboard model house look incredibly futuristic, covered in green fake moss and sleek glass windows.
Pitching the idea to the Principal to install actual solar panels on the school roof to cut the monthly electricity bills.

Field_Ecologist.title: The Wild Explorer (Field Ecologist / Wildlife Biologist)
Field_Ecologist.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on adventurer! You love being outdoors, aren't afraid of dirt or bugs, and want to physically protect the earth's natural ecosystems.
Field_Ecologist.day_in_the_life: Trekking through the Western Ghats, taking soil and water samples, tracking wild elephants, and rescuing injured wildlife from cities.
Field_Ecologist.alternative_match_text: Your love for active, outdoor work makes you a great fit for a Forest Ranger (IFS), Marine Biologist, or Veterinarian.
Field_Ecologist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCB is highly recommended). Degree: B.Sc in Environmental Science, Zoology, or Forestry. Next Steps: Pursue an M.Sc from top institutes like the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) or NCBS.

Climate_Analyst.title: The Green Geek (Climate Data Analyst / Researcher)
Climate_Analyst.primary_match_text: You have a highly logical and analytical brain. You want to save the planet, but you know that real change requires understanding the hard facts, math, and satellite data.
Climate_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Sitting with advanced software to analyze ISRO satellite weather data, forecasting pollution (AQI) levels, and mapping out the effects of climate change on Indian agriculture.
Climate_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your mathematical mindset means you'd also excel as a Meteorologist, Data Scientist, or Geoinformatics Engineer.
Climate_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM/PCB) or Humanities with Geography/Math. Degree: B.Sc in Environmental Science, Geography, or Statistics. Next Steps: Pursue a Master's in Climate Science, Geoinformatics, or Data Analytics.

Wildlife_Filmmaker.title: The Eco-Artist (Wildlife Filmmaker / Green Architect)
Wildlife_Filmmaker.primary_match_text: You are a creative soul who sees the deep beauty in nature. You believe that to save the environment, you must make people fall in love with it through art, design, or film.
Wildlife_Filmmaker.day_in_the_life: Shooting breathtaking tiger documentaries in Kanha National Park, or designing stunning eco-friendly homes that use natural wind for cooling instead of ACs.
Wildlife_Filmmaker.alternative_match_text: If not directly in environmental science, your creativity would make you an amazing Landscape Architect, Photojournalist, or UI/UX Designer.
Wildlife_Filmmaker.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (PCM required for Architecture). Degree: Bachelor of Design (B.Des), B.Arch, or BA in Mass Communication. Next Steps: Build a portfolio in wildlife photography or sustainable design.

Sustainability_Director.title: The Eco-Boss (NGO Director / Sustainability Consultant)
Sustainability_Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader with a mind for business and management. You know that to truly save the planet, you have to change how big companies and governments spend their money.
Sustainability_Director.day_in_the_life: Advising huge corporations (like Tata or Reliance) on how to reduce their plastic waste, managing multi-crore NGO funds, and leading nationwide tree-planting CSR campaigns.
Sustainability_Director.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and negotiation skills would make you a brilliant Corporate Lawyer, Public Policy Maker, or MBA Executive.
Sustainability_Director.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Humanities (Economics is a big plus). Degree: BBA, B.Com, or BA Economics. Next Steps: Pursue an MBA in Sustainability Management (from institutes like TERI) or a Master's in Public Policy.
